title: SheSaid 2026: The Global Story Continues, One Voice at a Time
content:
The #SheSaid campaign 2026 officially launched on 1 September and will run until 31 December 2026. Now in its seventh edition, #SheSaid continues to grow as a global campaign, bringing together participants from around the world to add and improve women’s voices on Wikimedia projects.

As part of Wiki Loves Women, an initiative of Wiki in Africa, #SheSaid works to address the gender gap on Wikiquote by making women’s words, experiences and perspectives more visible and accessible.

This year is particularly special: Wiki Loves Women is celebrating 10 years of making women visible in the world’s largest open knowledge ecosystem. #SheSaid is part of this decade-long journey, building on the contributions of thousands of participants who have helped bring women’s voices into the Wikimedia movement and beyond.

Six editions. More than 42k contributions. 22 languages from English to Assamese. More than 25 communities from Indonesia to Italy, Ghana and beyond. . 

#SheSaid is more than just the numbers. It is a story of people coming together across languages, countries and cultures, united by one purpose: to make women’s voices more visible.

title: Investing in Leadership Development at Every Stage Matters for Community Growth
content:
A reflection from Wikimedia Kenya User Group on why skills development, shared leadership and opportunities for growth are essential to building resilient communities.

There was a point during Wikimedia Kenya User Group’s recent team-building day when somewhere between the conversations, laughter and uncomfortable moments of reflection, the room changed. The titles and responsibilities that usually defined us seemed to fall away, and for a while, we were simply what we had spent years trying to build: a community.

We spent the day competing in well-crafted games, laughing at our desperate attempts to win and the missteps that cost us points, while discovering just how differently each of us approaches a challenge. But beneath the fun, the activities revealed something more important; they showed us how much we rely on trust, communication and listening to work towards a common goal, and how leadership is not always about taking charge, but also about knowing when to step back and make space for someone else.
snippet: A reflection from Wikimedia Kenya User Group on why skills development, shared leadership and opportunities for growth are essential to building resilient communities.
creator: Ms Kabintie

title: Wikiscout: Empowering young people in Tunisia through scouting and Wikimedia
content:
In Tunisia, an innovative partnership is bringing together two dynamic communities with a shared vision: empowering young people through knowledge, skills, and civic engagement. WikiScout is a collaborative project between the Tunisian Scouts and the Wikimedia Tunisia User Group, designed to introduce young scouts to Wikimedia projects while reinforcing their connection to their local environments.

The initiative builds on the strengths of both movements. Scouting has long been rooted in community service, teamwork, and personal development, while Wikimedia projects offer an open platform for sharing knowledge with the world. By combining these approaches, WikiScout creates a meaningful learning experience that is both practical and impactful.

The project began with a series of workshops organized in different cities across Tunisia, including Sfax, Gafsa, and Sbeitla. These initial activities serve as pilot experiences to test methodologies, build local capacity, and engage young participants in contributing to Wikimedia platforms. Over the next two years, WikiScout aims to expand progressively to reach scout groups across the entire country.

title: Wikimedia Spain unveils its new visual identity in 2026 and updates its graphic resources
content:
In 2026, Wikimedia Spain is unveiling an evolution of its visual identity, with the aim of creating a new image that is clearer, more consistent and more versatile across its various communication channels and materials. 

The new identity retains the essence of Wikimedia Spain and seeks to strengthen its presence as an association, whilst offering a visual image that is more consistent with Wikimedia and with the range of projects and communities that form part of its movement. 

The update does not represent a radical change to the brand, but rather an evolution of its visual elements to make it easier to apply in different contexts. 

The main objectives of this evolution include: 

  • Strengthening the image of Wikimedia Spain. 
  • Improving visual consistency with the Wikimedia Movement. 
  • Making it easier to use the brand identity in projects, activities and collaborations. 
  • To have clearer and more consistent graphic resources for communication. 

    • The update includes various resources to facilitate the implementation of the new visual identity by Wikimedia Spain and by the  individuals and organisations that collaborate with the association. 

    These include: 

  • Logo and isotypes. 
  • Updated visual identity manual.

title: The First Time My Code Was Merged into Open Source, I Felt Like I Belonged
content:
This summer I participated as a Google Summer of Code 2026 contributor with support from the Wikimedia Foundation building a Bulk Ocr review workflow feature for Wikisource. It was three months that changed how I see myself as a developer. Here is what I built, the moments that stayed with me and the lessons I will carry forward. My full technical report with links to every change is on mediawiki.org.

I have been part of the Wikimedia movement since 2021, when I started as a volunteer editor. Over time I became an administrator( sysop) on Swahili Wikipedia where I review edits, help and mentor new contributors and and improve Swahili content. Being an administrator taught me how much a strong community and good tools matter to the volunteers who build free knowledge everyday.

Wikisource is a free online library where volunteers turn scanned books into text people can read and search. A tool called OCR turns each scanned page image into text and Bulk OCR lets volunteers run OCR on many pages at once instead of one at a time.

title: Meet the visual identity of WikiConference India 2026
content: As Wikimedians from across India and South Asia prepare to meet in Kochi this September, WikiConference India 2026 is taking shape not only through its program and participants, but also through a visual identity designed to reflect the spirit of the conference. From the logo that will appear across conference materials to the mascot that will accompany participants through the event, these visual elements are intended to make WCI 2026 feel recognisable, welcoming, and distinctly connected to the place where we are coming together. A logo communicates a variety of important ideas with a few visual elements; that was the idea the design team of WikiConference India 2026 had in mind when they began to work on its logo to represent the themes of the conference, the current discussions around the Wikimedia ecosystem, and the hopes and expectations behind planning this conference. The resulting logo also aims to demonstrate the continuity of the Wikiconference India and Indic Wikimedia communities over the years, the breadth of cultural diversity that India carries, and the unique identity of Kochi city- the location where the conference is being held.

title: Call for Presenters: Japan Wikimedia Conference 2026!
content:
The Wikimedians of Japan User Group (WJPUG) is calling for presenters for the Japan Wikimedia Conference 2026, to be held on Sunday, December 6, 2026, at the Keio University Mita Campus in Minato Ward, Tokyo. This conference aims to facilitate networking and the exchange of knowledge among individuals involved in the Wikimedia movement—both in Japan and abroad—as well as those who utilize Wikimedia projects and resources.

We aim to foster greater activity, collaboration, mutual support, and new initiatives by bringing together a diverse group of people—including contributors to various Wikimedia projects, those involved in offline activities like outreach, individuals utilizing Wikimedia content in their services, and even those simply interested in Wikimedia—to engage in discussion and the exchange of information.

title: This Month at WMGH (August 2026): Wikimedia and Pop Culture, Giveaways and Regional Wikipedia Workshops Ahead
content:
In August, the Wikimedia Ghana User Group continued creating spaces for learning and participation within the Wikimedia movement. We brought Wikimedia to pop-culture enthusiasts, hosted a Wikimania 2026 swag giveaway, and prepared to resume our regional Wikipedia 101 workshops for the 2026/2027 fiscal year. We also have some new tools to share with the community!

Here’s what we’ve been up to!

On 22 August 2026, we participated in the Nerd Con Accra Expo at the Goethe-Institut Ghana to bring Wikimedia to an audience of pop culture enthusiasts focused on gaming, anime, film and other digital interests.

We set up a booth to engage attendees about Wikimedia projects and ways to get involved and also hosted a Wikipedia 101 workshop. The event provided an opening to engage a youthful, technology-oriented audience whose interests align closely with opportunities to contribute to the Wikimedia movement.

title: Entering Our Third Phase: How WCB 3.0 Nurtures West Java’s Cultural Heritage Preservation Through Wikimedia Projects
content:
“Cultural heritage isn’t about historical scripts or buildings; it’s about our identity.”

 “Cultural heritage isn’t about historical scripts or buildings; it’s about our identity.”

Reflecting on our journey with the WCB project from 2024 to 2025, we are taking the next step in our mission to turn Sundanese historical and cultural archives into open knowledge, accessible to everyone in digital spaces.

WCB 3.0 was initiated by the Wikimedia Bandung community to document cultural heritage in West Java and Banten through the Wikimedia projects, integrating initiatives across Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, Sundanese Wikipedia, Indonesian Wikipedia, and supported by a rapid fund from the Wikimedia Foundation.

In this third phase, the project was led by three core members of the Wikimedia Bandung community: User:Lany pirna, User:Mirani Pramitasari, and User:Pijri Paijar. We expanded our documentation coverage to include the City and Regency of Bandung, Cimahi, Bandung Barat, Cianjur, Tasikmalaya, Cirebon, Majalengka, Subang, and Banten.

title: Archiving the Present, a network for South Asia’s oral knowledge launches in Kochi before WikiConference India
content:
On 3 September, 37 of us are meeting to learn from each other how we can better document our community stories, voices and knowledge and safe-keep them for long. Most have spent over three months learning together online and will meet in person for the first time.

This is the day OpenSpeaks, together with other collaborators, launches Archiving the Present, a community network for oral knowledge in local languages, a manual and a free course of the same name. The network—individual language documenters, archivists, groups and organisations representing local communities, language archives, media institutions, funders, and others—will support the documentation and archiving of South Asia’s languages.

The network will align with a shared goal—that oral knowledge is human knowledge and deserves to be treated as equal to written knowledge. That means fair recognition and fair pay for the people who hold it.

title: More than a campaign: the measurable impact of Celebrate Women 2026
content:
Imagine a world in which every woman on the planet finds a representative and diverse sum of all human knowledge about women+* available on Wikipedia and on the internet. This is what the Celebrate Women campaign has been trying to accomplish since 2022. 

Every March, during Women’s History Month and in celebration of International Women’s Day (March 8th), the Wikimedia community gathers both online and in person to edit and improve the content available on Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia projects about women+. The editing happens as part of edit-a-thons, workshops, training sessions, and many other types of gatherings, which are spread around the world, with events on every continent. 

For 2026, we had one of the biggest campaigns so far. Considering all the gatherings globally, we had 112 events listed on the official page, which were divided into these sections: 

  • Global: 21 events
  • Africa: 20 events
  • Asia: 15 events
  • Europe: 38 events
  • Latin America: 12 events
  • Middle East: 1 event
  • North America: 3 events
  • Oceania: 2 events
